final_resume.summary: Backend engineer with 3 years building Java and Spring Boot microservices for payments.

bullets: Reduced p95 latency of the settlement API from 800 ms to 350 ms by adding Redis caching.
Split the monolithic payouts module into 4 Spring Boot microservices communicating over REST.
Mentored 2 junior engineers and conducted code reviews in 2-week Agile sprints.
Implemented JPA/Hibernate repositories and MySQL schema changes for the merchant onboarding service.
Automated nightly reconciliation reports, saving the operations team 6 hours per week.

profile_improvement_tips: Gain hands-on experience with distributed systems concepts (consensus, eventual consistency, CAP theorem) and document them in a project or role description.
Study and apply common design patterns (Factory, Observer, Strategy, Circuit Breaker) in your microservices work, then highlight pattern usage in your resume.
Deepen algorithmic problem-solving skills through competitive programming or system design interviews; mention algorithmic optimisations in future backend work.
final_resume.growth_note: You meet the 3+ years professional experience requirement and have strong microservices and backend fundamentals. However, the JD emphasises distributed systems, algorithms, and design patterns as core competencies. Your resume currently demonstrates code review and microservices architecture but lacks explicit evidence of distributed systems design or algorithmic optimisation work. Gaining and showcasing these skills will significantly strengthen your candidacy for this level.
